editorial:
Imagine sitting in a living room with smart friends when one drops a bombshell that changes everything. That is the heart of this film. A college professor named John is packing up to leave town, and his colleagues gather for a goodbye party. Instead of small talk, John reveals he is actually a caveman who has lived for fourteen thousand years. The whole movie is one long conversation in a single room, but it never feels boring. The cast of professors, a doctor, and a student all react differently, and their questions pull you deeper into the story. You feel like you are right there on the couch, listening in.

Standout acting keeps the tension alive, especially the lead's calm, believable performance. The pacing is slow but steady, and the dialogue is sharp and thought-provoking. On the downside, the low budget shows, and there is almost no action or special effects. If you need explosions, this is not for you. But if you love big ideas and debates about history and faith, you will be hooked. It is best enjoyed streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, renting on Apple TV, or picking up the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: After the gathering, John leaves town with Sandy. Later, the skeptical psychiatrist calls and admits he now believes John, revealing his own father once taught alongside a man who never aged, which is John himself. This confirms John's impossible lifespan and shows his secret has been noticed before. John hangs up and drives into a new life, leaving his old identity behind.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves big ideas and deep conversations.
